user.title: Electrical Panel Capacity
user.description:
Enter the **per-phase fuse or breaker size** for your electrical panel in Amperes.

This is the maximum current each phase can carry before the breaker trips. You can usually find this labelled on the main breaker inside your electrical panel (e.g. 25 A, 32 A, 63 A).

**Tip:** For three-phase systems, enter the per-phase rating — not the total across all phases.

data_description.fuse_size: The ampere rating printed on your main circuit breaker for a single phase. Common values: 16 A, 20 A, 25 A, 32 A, 40 A, 63 A.

phases.title: Current Sensors
phases.description:
Assign a **current sensor** (measuring Amperes) to each phase you want to monitor. These are provided by energy monitors such as a Shelly EM, Eastron SDM, or a smart meter integration.

Only assign sensors to phases that actually exist in your installation. The **Monitor These Phases** checkboxes below control which assigned phases are actively watched — uncheck a phase to temporarily disable it without removing its sensor.

data_description.phase_1_sensor: A sensor entity whose state is the current draw in Amperes (or mA) for phase L1.
data_description.phase_2_sensor: A sensor entity whose state is the current draw in Amperes (or mA) for phase L2.
data_description.phase_3_sensor: A sensor entity whose state is the current draw in Amperes (or mA) for phase L3.
data_description.enabled_phases: Select which phases should trigger load-reduction actions. Phases without a sensor are ignored.

behavior.title: Reaction Behavior
behavior.description:
Control **when** and **how quickly** the load balancer reacts to overloads.

**Aggressiveness** sets the trigger threshold as a percentage of your {fuse_size} A fuse:
- **Very Low (100%)** — triggers at {very_low_trigger} A — acts only when the fuse limit is actually reached
- **Low (95%)** — triggers at {low_trigger} A — acts only when very close to the limit
- **Medium (90%)** — triggers at {medium_trigger} A — balanced, recommended for most homes
- **High (85%)** — triggers at {high_trigger} A — acts early, gives more headroom
- **Very High (80%)** — triggers at {very_high_trigger} A — most conservative, most protective

**Spike Filter** prevents the balancer from reacting to short-lived current spikes (e.g. motor startups, microwave ovens). The overload must be sustained for at least this many seconds before any action is taken. Recommended: 20–30 s.

**Restore Headroom** is the minimum free capacity (in Amperes) that must be available on all monitored phases before the balancer starts gradually restoring EV current or re-enabling toggled devices.

data_description.aggressiveness: Higher aggressiveness = lower trigger threshold = earlier intervention = more safety margin.
data_description.spike_filter_time: Minimum number of seconds a phase must remain overloaded before any load-reduction action is triggered. Prevents false reactions to momentary current spikes.
data_description.restore_headroom: Minimum free capacity (trigger threshold minus measured current) that must be present on all monitored phases before any load is restored. Default: 3 A. Increase for a more conservative safety buffer; decrease if your loads are stable and you want faster restoration.

actions.title: Load Reduction & Notifications
actions.description:
Define what happens when a sustained overload is detected.

**EV / Charging Control:** Select a `number` entity that controls charging current. The integration steps it down during overload and gradually restores it once load is clear.

**Devices to Toggle Off:** Turned off, in the order listed, if throttling the charger alone is not enough. Restored automatically when the overload clears.

**Notifications:** When enabled, an alert appears in the HA dashboard (bell icon). Select your phone from the **Notification Device** dropdown to also receive a push notification.

Everything can be changed later via **Configure**, which also offers restore priority, timing and other advanced settings.

data.devices_to_toggle: Devices to Turn Off During Overload

data_description.charging_entity: A `number` entity that sets the charging current in Amperes. Works with any EVSE that exposes a current-control number entity (Tesla, Wallbox, go-e, etc.).
data_description.devices_to_toggle: Switches, climate units, water heaters, fans or input booleans. Turned off in the order listed when reducing charging current is not enough, and turned back on in reverse order (climate and water heaters return to their previous mode).
data_description.notify_enabled: When enabled, an overload alert is posted to the Home Assistant notification centre (bell icon) and optionally to your phone. Turn off to suppress all overload notifications.
data_description.notify_target: Select your phone or tablet from the list. Only devices with the Home Assistant companion app installed and push notifications registered will appear. Leave unset for dashboard-only notifications.

error.duplicate_sensor: The same sensor is assigned to more than one phase.
error.no_monitored_phase: Assign a sensor to at least one phase and tick that phase under Monitor These Phases.

init.title: Load Balancer Settings
init.description: Choose which group of settings to change. Changes take effect immediately — any reduction or restoration in progress continues.

thresholds.title: Fuse Size & Reaction Thresholds
thresholds.description: With the current {fuse_size} A fuse the aggressiveness levels trigger at: Very Low {very_low_trigger} A · Low {low_trigger} A · Medium {medium_trigger} A · High {high_trigger} A · Very High {very_high_trigger} A.

data_description.fuse_size: The ampere rating of your per-phase circuit breaker.
data_description.aggressiveness: Higher aggressiveness triggers load reduction earlier (lower threshold).
data_description.spike_filter_time: Seconds the overload must persist before any action is taken.
data_description.restore_headroom: Minimum free capacity (trigger threshold minus measured current) required on all monitored phases before any load is restored. Default: 3 A.

sensors.title: Current Sensors
sensors.description: Assign a current sensor (A or mA) to each phase and choose which phases are monitored.

data_description.phase_1_sensor: Current draw for phase L1. Clear the field to remove it.
data_description.phase_2_sensor: Current draw for phase L2. Clear the field to remove it.
data_description.phase_3_sensor: Current draw for phase L3. Clear the field to remove it.
data_description.enabled_phases: Only ticked phases with a sensor trigger load reduction.

load_control.title: EV Charger & Devices
load_control.description: What gets reduced during an overload, and in which order it comes back. Load that is currently reduced is still restored if you remove it here.

data.devices_to_toggle: Devices to Turn Off During Overload

data_description.charging_entity: A `number` (or `input_number`) entity that sets the charging current in Amperes. Reduced first, because it can be adjusted in small steps.
data_description.devices_to_toggle: Turned off in the order listed when reducing the charger is not enough; turned back on in reverse order.
data_description.device_load: How many Amperes one device is assumed to draw. Used to decide how many devices to turn off at once, and how much headroom (this value plus Restore Headroom) is needed before a device is turned back on. Set it to roughly the per-phase current of your largest device.
data_description.restore_priority: Which load comes back first once there is room. The other waits until the first is fully restored.

data_description.notify_enabled: Toggle all notifications on or off. An overload alert is posted to the Home Assistant notification centre (bell icon) and optionally to your phone.
data_description.notify_target: Select your mobile device to receive push notifications. Only devices with the HA companion app appear here. Clear the field for dashboard-only notifications.
data_description.notify_on_restore: Also send a message when the overload is over and all reduced load is back. On your phone it replaces the overload alert.

advanced.title: Advanced Timing
advanced.description: Fine-tune the control loop. The defaults suit most homes.

data_description.restore_settle_time: Headroom must be continuously available this long before the first restore step. Default: 60 s.
data_description.restore_step_time: Wait between restore steps (one charger step or one device), giving each step time to show its effect. Default: 60 s.
data_description.reduction_interval: Minimum time between load-reduction actions during an overload, so the charger has time to react before more is cut. Default: 10 s.
data_description.charger_margin: Amperes removed from the charger on top of the measured overload, for a safety buffer. Default: 2 A.

error.duplicate_sensor: The same sensor is assigned to more than one phase.
error.no_monitored_phase: Assign a sensor to at least one phase and tick that phase under Monitor These Phases.
